title: VehicleSetupCompletionResponse
description: The 200 body of POST /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/complete-setup (rest-api.md §7.23, contracts v0.25.0) — the ACTION half of the setupState surfaces MYR-491 put on §7.0 and §7.1. WHY IT IS A SEPARATE SCHEMA AND NOT A REUSE: the object is the same shape, but the CONTRACT AROUND IT is deliberately stronger in two ways that a shared schema could not express. (1) `setupState` here is NEVER null — a passive read may make no claim, but a request that asked the server to finish setting up a car always gets an answer, and null would be useless to the client rendering the progress card. (2) The `state` enum is a SUPERSET: it carries `streaming`, the positive member §7.0/§7.1 deliberately lack (MYR-491: 'null is NOT ready — there is no ready member'), because on this surface the server has just looked at the car's status and freshness and does know. THE SERVER NEVER EMITS `streaming` ON §7.0 OR §7.1, and a consumer must not expect it there. Every other member means exactly what it means on the read surfaces, produced by the same server-side helpers, so the two can never disagree about one vehicle. FAILURE IS NEVER A STATE: every way this endpoint can fail is a typed HTTP error (§7.23's table) and no error response carries a setupState at all, so a client renders a retry affordance from the code rather than a setup card. SHARED WITH §7.29 (MYR-599, contracts v0.39.0; the endpoint is documented at rest-api.md §7.29 — §7.24 is ride-requests/join, and the v0.39.0 text naming §7.24 was wrong): `POST /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/acknowledge-owner-approval` returns THIS SAME SHAPE, deliberately, so a client reuses its existing completion handling verbatim — record the acknowledgment, run the same best-effort config push complete-setup runs, answer with the vehicle's resulting setupState. See `$defs.AcknowledgeOwnerApprovalRequest` for that endpoint's request body and its full contract.

vehicleId.description: The Prisma cuid the request addressed, echoed back so a client completing several vehicles can attribute each answer. NOT a VIN — a full VIN never crosses this wire (§1.3, §2.1).

setupState.description: What now stands between this vehicle and live telemetry, as of this request. NEVER null on this surface — contrast VehicleState.setupState / VehicleSummary.setupState, where null is the ordinary 'no claim' answer. Same two members and the same semantics; one shared server-side derivation, so a completion response and the next snapshot cannot contradict each other.

state.description: `streaming` — the car is sending live telemetry; setup is COMPLETE and nothing further is required. THIS MEMBER IS EXCLUSIVE TO §7.23/§7.29 and is never emitted on §7.0/§7.1. `awaiting_owner_acknowledgment` (MYR-599, contracts v0.39.0) — the car was linked by someone holding DRIVER access on Tesla's side and the owner-approval acknowledgment has NOT been recorded, so the server refused to push a telemetry config and is telling the client what is missing rather than inventing progress. THE LINKER MUST ACT: present the acknowledgment sheet and POST §7.29. Reachable from §7.23 as well as §7.29 — complete-setup on an unacknowledged driver car returns this state instead of pushing — and it SORTS BEFORE `owner_access_required` / `configuring` / `awaiting_virtual_key` / `token_failed`, because consent precedes both pairing evidence and any push. From §7.29 it is the answer to a call whose acknowledgment did not stick; the ordinary §7.29 answer is the NEXT state — `owner_access_required` for as long as Tesla refuses driver-token config creation, and `awaiting_virtual_key` / `configuring` if that ever changes. `owner_access_required` (MYR-599, contracts v0.40.0) — the config push this call attempted was REFUSED BY TESLA: the account that linked the car holds DRIVER access, and Tesla's Fleet API lets ONLY the vehicle's OWNER account create a telemetry config. It is the ordinary answer from §7.29 for a driver-access car whose acknowledgment has just been recorded, and from §7.23 for one acknowledged earlier — the acknowledgment stuck, the push did not, and no HTTP error could say so honestly because the endpoint itself did not fail. NEITHER THE CLIENT NOR THE LINKER CAN RETRY OUT OF IT: copy MUST NOT offer 'reconnect Tesla' (that is `token_failed`'s action) — the honest action is for the car's Tesla OWNER to add the car in MyRoboTaxi under their OWN account and share it with the driver. `since` = when the refusal was observed. It SORTS AFTER `awaiting_owner_acknowledgment`, the only state it can follow, and BEFORE `configuring` / `awaiting_virtual_key` / `token_failed`, because a definitive refusal is not progress and 'waiting for the car' would be fabricated. The server emits it only on POSITIVE EVIDENCE — a driver-access row, an acknowledgment on record, and the config POST's generic 404 `<VIN> not_found` seen while the SAME token's vehicle list still carries the VIN — never from a bare 404, which a revoked grant also returns. If Tesla ships DRIVER-token config POST ('coming soon' per teslamotors/fleet-telemetry#116 and #126, 2024-03-14; no announcement says it shipped as of 2026-09-05), the next push succeeds and this member simply stops being emitted — consumers need no change. `configuring` — the virtual key is confirmed enrolled and the fleet-telemetry config has been pushed, either by this call or earlier in the same pairing epoch; NO OWNER ACTION, the client narrates progress and may suggest waking the car's screen if it persists. `awaiting_virtual_key` — Tesla reports the virtual key is NOT enrolled on the vehicle; THE OWNER MUST ACT, and because the client knows it just sent them to the Tesla app it should surface the pairing retry proactively rather than leaving them to discover a dead control (MYR-503). `token_failed` — the owner's Tesla authorization can no longer be resolved or refreshed; THE OWNER MUST ACT (reconnect the Tesla account). NOTE WHAT IS ABSENT: there is no member for 'we could not tell'. A car whose pairing Tesla would not report, a car that would not wake, and a config push that failed are all typed HTTP errors, because a confident wrong answer on a card whose job is naming the ONE thing left to do is worse than no answer. New members may be added in a minor version; consumers MUST treat an unrecognised value as 'setup is incomplete, reason unknown' and MUST NOT fail the decode.

since.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant at which the evidence behind `state` was recorded — the last live frame for `streaming`, the forced re-push or the pairing epoch it belongs to for `configuring`, and this read for `awaiting_virtual_key` / `token_failed`. It is DATA FOR THE COPY ('for 2 minutes'), NOT an input a consumer re-derives `state` from. Never zero and never in the future: the server floors it at the read instant, so a client may subtract it from `now` without guarding for a negative age.

AcknowledgeOwnerApprovalRequest.title: AcknowledgeOwnerApprovalRequest
AcknowledgeOwnerApprovalRequest.description: The request body of `POST /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/acknowledge-owner-approval` (rest-api.md §7.29, MYR-599, contracts v0.39.0 — v0.39.0 cited §7.24 for this endpoint and that was wrong: §7.24 is `POST /api/ride-requests/join`) — the consent gate in front of provisioning a car its linker DRIVES but does not OWN on Tesla's side. WHY THE ENDPOINT EXISTS: a driver-access vehicle IS provisioned (the row is created, the virtual key the person already paired is not wasted), but NOTHING is pushed to the car — no fleet-telemetry config, no reconnect, no keepalive re-push — until the person who linked it states that the owner approved adding it. The vehicle reads `setupState.state` = 'awaiting_owner_acknowledgment' and `teslaAccessType` = 'driver' until then. AUTH AND OWNERSHIP: bearer, and the caller must own the platform's Vehicle row — the SAME ownership check as §7.23 complete-setup, but NOT the same answer when it fails, and the v0.39.0 text asserting otherwise was wrong. THIS endpoint answers 404 `not_found` for both an unknown vehicle and one owned by somebody else, so it cannot be used to probe which vehicleIds exist. §7.23 complete-setup DOES distinguish them: 403 `vehicle_not_owned` on a real ownership mismatch, 404 `not_found` only for a vehicle that does not exist or is ownership-filtered (matching §7.12 / §7.14 / §7.15). A client MUST NOT treat the two endpoints' ownership failures as interchangeable. IDEMPOTENT BY DESIGN: a second call on an already-acknowledged car is a 200, never a 409 — it re-runs the same best-effort config push and returns the vehicle's current setupState, which makes it a safe retry for a client that lost the first response, and a usable 'try again' for a push that failed transiently. The stored acknowledgment is NOT overwritten into something weaker: the first acknowledgment's instant is what the platform would point to if an owner ever complained. OWNER-ACCESS CARS ARE A 200 NO-OP: a vehicle whose `teslaAccessType` is 'owner' has nothing to acknowledge, so the call records nothing, pushes nothing new and returns the setupState the normal derivation yields — a client that cannot tell the two cases apart is never punished for asking. RESPONSE: VehicleSetupCompletionResponse, the SAME shape §7.23 returns (`vehicleId`, non-null `setupState`), so the client's existing completion handling is reused unchanged. As of contracts v0.40.0 the usual answer for a driver-access car is `owner_access_required` — Tesla will not let a driver token create the config at all, so the acknowledgment is recorded and the push is refused in the same breath; `awaiting_virtual_key`, with the existing pair-key card taking over, is what the call answers once Tesla permits the push. FAILURE IS NEVER A STATE, exactly as on §7.23: every way this can fail is a typed HTTP error and no error body carries a setupState.

acknowledgmentVersion.description: The version id of the acknowledgment text the client ACTUALLY RENDERED, verbatim, on the sheet the person confirmed. The canonical text and its id ship with this contracts package (`owner-approval-v1`); a client MUST send the id of the copy it displayed and MUST NOT invent, abbreviate or re-word one — the whole point of storing it is that the platform can later say WHICH words a person agreed to. The server stores this string and the instant, and NOTHING ELSE about the acknowledgment; it does not validate the text, only that the id is present and within length. An id the server does not recognise is still recorded as sent, because a client shipped before a copy revision must not be blocked from finishing setup. Format is a lowercase slug with a version suffix; treat it as an OPAQUE token, never parse it for ordering. P0: a consent-record version marker, carrying no personal data — the person is identified by the authenticated caller, not by anything in this body.
